documents.title: Types of Violations (Academic Integrity Policy, incl. AI-Generated Work)
documents.stance_why: The AI-Generated Work entry says AI-generated work "is not acceptable, unless authorized specifically by the instructor/administrator". That bans AI by default and allows it only when an instructor or administrator authorizes it, so the stance is restrict.
documents.summary: A list of academic integrity violation categories. Only two passages concern AI: plagiarism is defined to cover AI-generated sources, and 'AI-Generated Work' is its own violation, unacceptable unless the instructor or administrator authorizes it. The rest of the page (cheating, fabrication, technological misconduct) does not mention AI.

units.why: The sentence lists AI-generated work as an integrity violation category and says it is "not acceptable, unless authorized specifically by the instructor/administrator". This is a default ban with an authorization exception, which is the fallback rule when no authorization exists (P06). P36 also fits but the sentence's operative content is the default-unless-authorized rule.
units.anchor: is not acceptable, unless authorized specifically by the instructor/administrator

units.why: The clause gives the reason for the ban: AI-generated work "is not reflective of a student’s own understanding and effort". It explains the restriction as protecting the student's own learning and effort, so it is a rationale (informs) and fits P41 better than P29, which is about owning submitted work.
units.anchor: not reflective of a student’s own understanding and effort

units.why: The plagiarism definition says it "applies to any type of source, whether published or unpublished, human or AI-generated". This treats AI output as a source under existing plagiarism rules, so it is P45 (AI as an outside source under existing rules) and not P36, since it defines scope rather than a sanction.
units.anchor: human or AI-generated, and to any type of assignment

units.why: Since plagiarism covers AI-generated sources, the rule that submitted work with others' material "must include complete, accurate, and specific references" and quotation marks for verbatim text requires citing it. This is a disclosure and citation requirement (P24), not the detailed tool/prompt citation of P25, because no such details are named.
units.anchor: must include complete, accurate, and specific references
units.frag_start: Any assignment submitted by a student
units.policy: Any assignment submitted by a student that includes the words, ideas, data, or creative works of another must include complete, accurate, and specific references; plagiarism applies to AI-generated sources.

units.why: The page lists AI-Generated Work among the violations of "IUP’s standards of academic integrity", so unauthorized AI use is classed as academic misconduct under the integrity policy. This is P36.
units.anchor: Violations of IUP’s standards of academic integrity include
units.frag_start: Violations of IUP’s standards of academic
units.policy: AI-Generated Work is one of the categories of violations of IUP's standards of academic integrity.

notes: Thin source: one university-level page with a single AI clause plus the AI mention in the plagiarism definition. Topic codes were chosen without AGENT_BRIEF.md and may need mapping.
